extracted.intended_audience: advocates, practitioners, and researchers drafting public comments on agency rulemakings (e.g., EPA commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting public (notice-and-comment) submissions intended to influence final regulatory rule stringency by engaging the causal channels agencies use (cost-benefit analysis, technical feasibility, political signals, and usable drafting input).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative data affecting the cost-benefit calculus
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment provide quantitative data affecting the cost-benefit calculus?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magat et al. identify cost-benefit characteristics as a predictor of final rule stringency; effective comments should provide cost or benefit data that affects the agency's CBA channel (e.g., numbers, estimates, empirical studies). This is distinct from purely qualitative claims — the emphasis is on data that can be incorporated into the agency's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document operational feasibility or infeasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment document operational feasibility or infeasibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies consider technical and operational feasibility when finalizing rules. Provide concrete documentation (tests, pilot results, engineering assessments) showing whether proposed standards can be implemented in practice or why they cannot, so agency staff can evaluate feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marshal evidence of political support
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment marshal evidence of political support (other commenters, congressional letters, public opinion)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The political environment predicts rule outcomes. Comments that demonstrate broader political backing or visible stakeholder coalitions — via coordinated filings, endorsements, letters from officials, or public-opinion evidence — make the political salience of an issue clearer to agency leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide drafting input agency staff could use
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment provide drafting input agency staff could use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency staff value submissions that are directly usable for drafting (e.g., suggested regulatory text, clear legal citations, articulated implementation language, templates). Supplying concrete, staff-ready language or methods increases the chance staff will incorporate changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to a coherent record across multiple causal channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment contribute to building a coherent record across multiple causal channels?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magat et al. emphasize that comments are most effective when they operate within a coherent set of political, analytical, and technical inputs. Effective strategy: align data, feasibility evidence, legal argument, and political signals so the comment augments other influences rather than acting in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize influence comes from contributing to a web of factors, not single-factor persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment recognize that influence often comes from contributing to a web of factors, not single-factor persuasion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single comments rarely shift rules alone. Comments should be designed to plug into existing analytical, political, and technical dynamics — i.e., aim to change one or more causal channels and complement other inputs rather than relying on lone persuasive appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for the anchoring effect of the initial proposal's stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment take into account the initial proposal's stringency (anchoring effect)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magat et al. found that the initial proposal's stringency predicts final outcomes (an anchoring effect). Effective comments should assess whether the proposal's baseline makes stricter or looser outcomes plausible and tailor arguments (e.g., feasibility or cost data) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the volume and direction of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the strategy consider both the volume and directional balance of comments received?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume and direction (pro vs. con) of comments were empirical predictors of final stringency. Strategies should aim not only for high-volume filings but also for demonstrating the direction of support through coordinated submissions, representative sampling, or highlighting key opposing comment clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address cost-benefit characteristics beyond raw numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment address broader cost-benefit characteristics (not just isolated data points)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond supplying quantitative data, comments should situate those numbers within the agency's cost-benefit framework: explain assumptions, counteragency estimates, show sensitivity analyses, or provide alternate valuation approaches so the agency can integrate them into its CBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and respond to the political environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment strategy assess and, where possible, influence the relevant political environment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political environment is a predictor of final outcomes. Comments can signal political salience (e.g., by coordinating stakeholder letters, engaging elected officials) or document external pressures affecting agency choices; tailor timing and content to current political dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make arguments usable by agency staff judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment facilitate favorable agency staff judgment by being clear, actionable, and technically grounded?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency staff judgment matters; present evidence and arguments in ways staff can evaluate quickly (executive summaries, clear citations, concise technical appendices). Focus on clarity and usability to increase uptake by staff reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document industry technological capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment document industry technological capacity (what is and isn't technically feasible within industry)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry technological capacity was identified as a predictor of final stringency. Provide surveys, adoption timelines, pilot program results, or manufacturer's data showing current capabilities and likely trajectories to inform agency assessments.
